newsitem.title: NORWAY: CHS Eletronic offers to take over Santech.
newsitem.headline: CHS Eletronic offers to take over Santech.

text.p: CHS Electronics Inc of the United States has offered to take over Norwegian hardware distributor Santech Micro Group ASA (SMG), Santech said in a statement to the Oslo Bourse on Monday.
Miami-based CHS, which is listed on Nasdaq, is offering to buy Santech for 20.50 crowns per share, valuing the company at 910 million crowns ($118.1 million), it said.
Santech said its board recommended shareholders to accept the bid. ($ = 7.706 Norwegian Crowns)
"The offer represents a premium of 38 percent compared to the final price of 14.90 crowns per share at the Oslo Bourse on Friday August 1," the statement said.
The acquisition is conditional of at least two-thirds of SMG shareholders accepting the offer, the successful completion of due diligence and formal approval by regulatory authorities, it said.
The offer will be formally submitted to shareholders this week and will stay valid for 14 days.
CHS, which is an international full-service distributor of computers, has a market capitalisation of $1.40 billion, SMG said.

"CHS today has a considerably lower turnover in Scandinavia than SMG, and wants to strengthen its position in this region significantly on the basis of SMG's market position and organisation," the statement said.

SMG said its second quarter pre-tax operating revenue fell to 965 million crowns from 971 million in the corresponding 1996 period. Pre-tax losses widened to 26 million crowns from 17 million, it said.
